source: REAL Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B Thinker inference on the W7900D during the repeatability runs of wsb_022_r0_s831023 (not synthetic tensors)
measurement: boundary tie = k-th and (k+1)-th ranked fp32 softmax probability EXACTLY equal at a routed token-slot; the selected expert set is then decided by the tie-break rule alone
findings: 18.35% of CPU-block and 20.20% of GPU-block routed token-slots sit on an exact top-k boundary tie: bf16 router logits quantise to few distinct values, making exact probability ties COMMON
the counts are bit-identical across all 5 runs (deterministic routing with the stable tie-break)

IMPLICATION: the stock torch.topk used by the stock HF loop is nondeterministic at these ties on torch 2.10.0+rocm7.14.1, i.e. roughly 1 in 5 routing decisions was previously run-to-run random - this is the quantified root cause of the RC5 pilot's placement-dependent score spread (5.0 / 4.83 / 4.83)

IMPLICATION for official equivalence: the official vLLM/CUDA fused-MoE kernel's tie rule is not known; with ~20% of slots tied, per-token expert CHOICE cannot be claimed equivalent to the official judge. Score-level equivalence remains unmeasured without a CUDA host (Q3O_OFFICIAL_EQUIVALENCE cannot be claimed)
torch_versions_tested_for_topk_nondeterm: 2.14.0+rocm10.1.0 (system env) - stable argsort used in all paths regardless; stock-topk behaviour not re-quantified here
stable_argsort_effect: selected expert set fixed deterministically (lowest index first); identical counts across processes A and B (fresh reload)
bf16_rounding_effect: router logits rounded to bf16 BEFORE routing (pinned by tests; mutation C2/R2 killed); unrounded fp32 logits would change both tie frequency and selection
